critique: The screen substantively fulfills the chess-interface brief: a complete 8×8 board contains all 32 pieces in recognizable standard starting ranks, coordinate markings appear around the board, and the side panel includes a White-to-move indicator, a move-history table, and three controls. The board and side UI share a coherent classic-club context. The principal fidelity issue is piece legibility and ownership: both sides use similar dark classic glyphs differentiated mostly by light versus dark square context and subtle outlines, so the white army does not read as crisply distinct from the black army. Several coordinate labels are also very small, weakening the explicit coordinate requirement.
suggestion: Preserve the exact 8×8 starting position and all 32 pieces, but give white and black pieces unmistakably different fills/outlines while retaining classic glyph silhouettes. Increase the rank/file coordinate labels enough to remain readable at the full 1280×800 view, and keep the turn indicator, move-history columns, New Match, Undo Move, and Flip Board controls visibly tied to the board. Do not alter the starting formation while improving ownership clarity.
